# Demo video — the narration, with real timings

*Generated by `npm run record:submission`. The timings below are the ones the recording in
`docs/demo/` actually has; they are written as the run happens, not planned in advance.*

The video is **captioned, not narrated** — the caption bar carries these lines. A voice track is
the presenter's to record, and these marks are what it should be laid against. The runtime of
the take this file describes is **3 min 56 s**.

Nothing in it is staged. The Hindi is a committed audio fixture played into a real microphone
stream; the Gemini call, the commit, the re-score, the ticket and the receipt all happen against
the running deployment while the camera is on. There is no cut anywhere in the take.

| Time | Line |
|---:|---|
| 0:07 | 12,010 facilities. 769 districts, 36 states. Tonight 16,772 stock positions are critical, and 20,511 positions are already at zero. |
| 0:13 | Every bubble is a district. Every arc is medicine that is already in the country, moving from where it will expire to where it will run out. |
| 0:22 | Bastar, Chhattisgarh. CHC Bastar-01 is short of Td Vaccine (Tetanus + Diphtheria) — a Vital drug — with a 100% chance of running out inside its resupply window. |
| 0:29 | The stock exists. CHC Nabarangpur-01 is 31 km away across the state line in Odisha, holding batch B009-HC001, which expires in 606 days. |
| 0:35 | But none of that is visible today, because the shelf is counted on paper. So we start there. |
| 0:43 | An ANM speaks her stock report in Hindi. No form, no app training, no typing. This is a real microphone stream into a real Gemini call. |
| 1:04 | Gemini transcribes it, translates it, and resolves each medicine against the catalogue. |
| 1:11 | Nothing is written yet. The draft is hers to confirm, and anything the model was unsure of is flagged rather than quietly accepted — a language model may not write into a national stock ledger unreviewed. |
| 1:18 | She confirms. The position is re-scored on the server in 14 milliseconds, appended to a durable log, and pushed to every open screen. |
| 1:30 | The national console. Her report is on it, marked as a live field report rather than as batch output, and it survives a reload — the page fetches the overlay on mount as well as subscribing to the stream. |
| 1:37 | Demand for all 36,143 district × drug series is forecast by Google's TimesFM, through BigQuery AI.FORECAST, 21 days ahead from a 90-day context — in concurrent statements that process zero bytes. |
| 1:44 | It does not serve every position, and that is measured rather than claimed: a 28-day held-out backtest gives TimesFM the demand class it wins by more than 5%. It holds 1,36,331 of 3,53,558 positions. We publish where it loses. |
| 1:51 | The same data carries the emergency signal. A tuned rule catches a doubled 14-day surge 100% of the time, a median 4.58 days before the first shelf empties — at 21% precision, which we publish because it is not flattering. |
| 2:00 | And one source is real. Kerala publishes a district-wise disease bulletin every day; 242 bulletins are read from their text layer, every column checked against its own total, and the same rule flags Kasaragod: fever, outpatient consultations, 2,485 against at most 1,932 — linked to the bulletin it came from. |
| 2:12 | The recommendation is not an alert. It names a batch, an expiry date, a distance and a price: 39 dose of Td Vaccine (Tetanus + Diphtheria) from CHC Nabarangpur-01, 31 km away, charged ₹931 because it shares a vehicle rather than ₹1,801 alone. |
| 2:20 | And it says who may issue it. This one crosses a state line, so an inter-state supply agreement has to be recorded first — the software refuses to let a district officer approve it on a signature alone. |
| 2:30 | Signed in as the officer who just recorded the agreement, Approve is refused: the same person cannot agree to an order and then sign it off. An officer of the receiving district has to. |
| 2:37 | Approved. Both ends are re-scored — as a projection, because approval moves no stock: medicine leaves the donor when it is dispatched and arrives when it is received. |
| 2:44 | Dispatched. Now the donor shelf actually falls — and no donor is ever taken past its own guardrail. |
| 2:52 | 36 arrived of 39 sent. The difference is kept as a variance and the receiver recovers by what turned up, not by what was posted. Most systems of this shape cannot represent that at all. |
| 3:03 | And the word the brief adds this year. 36 state nodes, each fitted on its own data. 56,660 numbers crossed a state line — against 65,05,740 consumption records that stayed where they were recorded. |
| 3:11 | Zero facility rows. Zero stock quantities. Zero patient records. Zero district identifiers. Every node is a URL you can fetch and hash for yourself, and the test suite sweeps all 36 files for leaks. |
| 3:18 | It is worth something, measured leave-one-state-out: a state joining with 30 days of its own history forecasts 36.0% closer to observed demand with the national prior than without it. |
| 3:27 | That is the artefact itself. Nothing here asks to be believed — it asks to be checked. |
| 3:35 | Districts, coordinates, LGD codes, Census populations, the essential medicines list and the IPHS norms are real. Facility-level stock is simulated, and labelled as simulated on every surface — because the absence of that data is the problem this is built for. |
| 3:43 | Gemini on Vertex AI. TimesFM in BigQuery. Cloud Run. All of it in asia-south1, and the forecast queries process zero bytes. |
| 3:49 | One state, eight weeks, two metrics: stock-out days prevented, and time from alert to action. Aarogya Grid. |
